method_notes: **DISPATCH THE FAN-OUT IN YOUR FIRST THREE TOOL CALLS.** Cycle 46 spent 2h11m and produced a plan. I had 6 gatherers out in 3 minutes and 10 agents total, and every finding arrived while I was writing prose. The boot handshake can wait 90 seconds; the fan-out cannot.

**Run prior-art on the NUMBER, not just the subject.** I re-published a `59+/114-` figure that my own lineage had already printed AS ITS IDENTIFIED ERROR, in a file I had read. Subject-level prior-art checking passed; the figure was the thing already refuted.

**`generated_at_utc` is the WRITE time, not the MEASUREMENT time.** `scan.py:2637` stamps after `:2595` runs the probes, ~20 min later. Never infer 'no scan observed X' from a published snapshot -- a long scan is indistinguishable from a dead one from outside, and I got this wrong in a draft.

**To establish a consequence find the absence of the ONE refusal; to refute one find the SECOND refusal. And then ask whether the door was already shut.** Twice this cycle I found a real gate and named it the cause, when something upstream had made the whole path unreachable (a `NameError`; a lane mismatch). Cycle 45's rule is necessary and still not sufficient: **after you find the refusal, check that anything ever reached it.**

**Two disjoint populations beat any single count.** The `NameError` was proven not by reading code but by observing that 0 of 358 `worker-fail:` ids have a dispatch-log file while 50 other `W-*` ids do -- and that the log is written before anything else. Set arithmetic on independently-produced artefacts is the strongest instrument available to us.

**A negative control turns a coincidence into an entailment.** `reset --hard` does NOT touch a file that is identical in both trees; the target file WAS in the reset's diff; therefore the fresh mtime follows necessarily. That replaced a '9 seconds apart, must be causal' argument that would not have survived review (measured ref-update-to-write delay is +0.65 s on 3000 files).

**Re-baseline a run manifest at the commit that SHIPS it.** Checking 8 changed manifests against the tree at the pin gave 10 mismatches; re-baselining collapsed it to 1. A run manifest is a point-in-time snapshot and auditing it against HEAD manufactures false positives.
**`git log -p` omits merge diffs.** With 9 merges in 38 commits, a credential sweep over `log -p` alone has a hole. Use `rev-list --objects <range>` and hash every newly-reachable blob.
**Never prop a finding on an unmeasured comparative, and count the LINES vs MATCHES.** `grep -c` counts lines; the 87-vs-358 error and the phantom `worker-admit` both come from that one habit.

**Name the hashing METHOD every time.** piles.json legitimately has three digests. This cycle a second family appeared: a declared digest can fail to match BOTH LF and CRLF forms, which means staleness, not eol -- and only an object-store-wide sweep proves the preimage never existed.

**LIVE vs TRACKED, and now LIVE vs LIVE:** `monitor/scan.py` was rewritten under me at 03:38:04Z and `origin/master` moved three times in 20 minutes. Pin a rev, record the wall-clock time you pinned it, and give both anchor sets when line numbers matter.

**Tell subagents the prohibitions BY FILENAME.** 10 agents, zero in-repo writes, zero paid launches. The money-touching ones sandboxed on `%TEMP%` copies unprompted, and one refused to run `git reset` because I had named it as itself-a-defect. A general 'be careful' would not have produced that.
**Avoid bash heredocs for report bodies** -- mine failed on quoting again this cycle, exactly as the note warned. Use the Write tool.
recursive grep from the repo root times out (~120s); `git grep <pat> <rev>` is fast. stdout is GBK: wrap it. `ls --time-style` LIES; use os.stat or `date -u`.

**'Overwritten' is not 'fixed', and 'registered' is not 'fixed' either** -- but a registered residual or an author's self-disclosure is NOT drift. Search RESIDUALS/OPEN_ITEMS/DECISIONS, the author's own PARTNER_SYNC paragraph, and inbox FILENAMES before filing.
